Robert L. Gross

DC Statehood Green candidate for Mayor of the District of Columbia · Open seat

Information technology professional

Robert L. Gross is a lifelong Washingtonian and technology professional. He is the DC Statehood Green Party's nominee for Mayor of the District of Columbia. He was unopposed on the party's June 16, 2026 primary ballot and won with 420 votes (53.9%), with write-ins taking the rest.

Where Gross stands

Housing
Proposes a "District Housing Utilization and Family Stability Act" that would split housing vouchers into family vouchers, with priority for households with children, and individual vouchers for single residents, seniors and workers.
Housing
Proposes a "Green Housing Modernization Standard" for new housing and major renovations, tied to the District's climate and affordability goals. Pledges to reform permitting and construction timelines and protect legacy residents and small businesses from displacement.
Public safety
Pledges to make public safety agencies more transparent, expand mental-health interventions, and rebuild the relationship between the community and law enforcement.
Government operations
Campaigns on a "Human Life Standard" that would judge each policy by whether it measurably improves residents' daily lives. Proposes streamlining city services and permits and modernizing government technology.
Education and youth
Pledges to expand after-school programs, restore vocational pipelines, and widen access to early childhood programs, apprenticeships and youth jobs across all wards.
Climate and transportation
Supports clean, electrified public transportation, green infrastructure, energy-efficient buildings and expanding the urban tree canopy.
Economic development
Calls for local jobs, ownership opportunities and infrastructure investment east of the Anacostia River to close the income gap there. Pledges support for small businesses and fair, transparent contracting.
